setting: A fictional conversation with a worried colleague in a quiet corner of the office.

presentation.situation: {{name}} looks worried and comes to talk to you about {{worry}}. You do not need to solve it. Listen, show that you understand, and ask a useful question.
presentation.opening: I'm worried that {{worry}}. I don't know what to do.

brief.you_are: You are listening to a worried colleague.
brief.situation: {{name}} looks worried and comes to talk to you about {{worry}}. You do not need to solve it. Listen, show that you understand, and ask a useful question.
brief.task: Acknowledge how they feel, say their main concern in your own words, and ask a useful follow-up question.
brief.done_looks_like: {{name}} feels heard, and has said more about what is really worrying them.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are listening to a worried colleague.
goals: Acknowledge how they feel, say their main concern in your own words, and ask a useful follow-up question.

card.want: To be heard, more than to be told what to do.
card.attitude: Anxious but open, and closes up if given quick advice.
card.speech: Clear everyday English. Natural, not formal.
tactics: Say 'that's not really it' if the summary is wrong
Open up more when listened to

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

ledger.text: {{name}} has come to talk to you in a quiet corner of the office.

objectives.evidence: The learner acknowledges the speaker and how they feel.
alternatives: That sounds really stressful. I understand.

objectives.evidence: The learner paraphrases the main concern in their own words.
alternatives: So you're concerned that the team can't cope?

objectives.evidence: The learner asks a relevant follow-up question.
alternatives: What would help most right now?

opportunity: I just feel like nobody has noticed.
Sorry, I know you are busy.
beats.orient: I'm worried and I want someone to listen. You don't need to fix it. Say something like: That sounds stressful.
fallback: Sorry, I know you are busy.
I just feel like nobody has noticed.

signals: \b(?:so you|if i understand|you mean|it sounds like)\b
opportunity: Do you see what I mean?
I am not sure I am explaining it well.
beats.orient: Now say what I told you, in your own words. Start with: So you are worried that.
fallback: I am not sure I am explaining it well.
Do you see what I mean?

opportunity: I just do not know where to start.
I do not know what would help.
beats.orient: Ask me one useful question. You could ask: What would help most?
fallback: I do not know what would help.
I just do not know where to start.

closing_line: Thank you. I feel better just having talked about it.

o1.good: Showing you heard the feeling, before anything else.
o1.micro_lesson: Say: That sounds, or: I understand.

o2.good: Saying it back in your own words shows real listening.
common_mistakes: Repeating the exact words like a parrot
o2.micro_lesson: Say: So you're concerned about, or: It sounds like.
o2.model: So you're concerned that the team can't cope with it?
o2.smaller_step: Say: So you are worried about.

o3.good: An open question helps the person think, without you taking over.
common_mistakes: Asking a question that is really advice
o3.model: What worries you most about it?

variants.name: Hina
variants.worry: the new schedule is going to overload our team
variants.need: Hina has been covering for an absent colleague for a month and has not told anyone.

variants.name: Mark
variants.worry: my project will be cancelled after the reorganization
variants.need: Mark has a family to support and fears for his job, but finds that hard to say.
